gaps.sentence: It would be ___ to take an umbrella — the sky is black.
gaps.explanation: 'Sensible' means showing good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected by things or feelings.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
gaps.hint: important enough to be remembered in history
gaps.explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: The children left ___ toys all over the floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Their' shows possession; 'there' is a place; 'they're' means 'they are'; 'theirs' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.

gaps.sentence: She is ___ of hearing after years beside the speakers.
gaps.explanation: 'Hard of hearing' is the fixed phrase; 'hardly' is an adverb.
